To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Individuals in distributed teams perceive that IT-enabled contextualization of information supports development of their collaboration know-how.

when individuals perceive the task they perform as nonroutine, the more they perceive their information technology (IT)-supported communication of context to be effective, the greater their collaboration know-how development.

1) IT support for communicating contextual information is positively related to individual collaboration know-how development when tasks are perceived as nonroutine; 2) partial IT support for communicating task contextual information is negatively related to individual collaboration development when tasks are routine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how IT can be used to support an individual's development of collaboration know-how in structurally diverse virtual teams.
the development of collaboration know-how through the communication of context information.
how IT-enabled contextualization of information affects the development of collaboration know-how of individuals working in distributed teams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
when individuals perceive the task as routine, IT support for contextual communication is not beneficial to the individual in terms of his collaboration know-how.
the more IT support for contextual communication, the higher the individual's perceived collaboration know-how development.

the results of this study indicate that when individuals in structurally diverse virtual teams perceive their task as being nonroutine, IT can be an effective tool in supporting their communication of contextual information to develop their collaboration knowledge-how, but when individuals perceive their tasks as routine, IT can hinder their communication of contextual knowledge and development of their collaboration knowledge-how.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of IT to enable contextualization can be effective in supporting collaboration know-how development in structurally diverse, distributed teams.
IT-enabled contextualization is a key factor in developing an individual's collaboration know-how.
the use of IT for supporting contextualization is a double-edged sword.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when IT supports contextualization, it can help develop the collaboration know-how of individuals in distributed teams.
IT support for contextualized communication is important for individuals to develop their collaboration skills in distributed settings.
IT-enabled contextualization can support the development of collaboration know-how for individuals working in structually diverse distributed teams.
